Throughout the week, Trump has repeatedly said he feels "super intelligence" is a more accurate term because the adjective "artificial" makes AI sound "fake."

item.title: Chinese FM comments on US' use of 'superintelligence' instead of 'artificial intelligence'
item.description:
The heads of state of China and the US held in-depth discussions on artificial intelligence during their meeting. Regarding the phrasing on artificial intelligence, China attaches importance to the US position and respects the phrase used by the US side, a Chinese FM spokesperson said on Saturday, commenting on the US' use of the term "superintelligence" instead of "artificial intelligence" when introducing the outcomes of the Chinese leader's visit to the US.
The spokesperson added that artificial intelligence technology is continuing to develop, and all parties can strengthen exchanges, deepen discussions and seek consensus in light of the latest developments.

item.title: Nearly 100 new laws take effect this week: Guns, artificial intelligence, facial recognition, ICE, and more
item.description:
In the fast-changing world of technology, the state legislature passed a package of consumer protections and privacy laws related to facial recognition, artificial intelligence, chatbots, and surveillance pricing, among others.
From [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence) [to guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glock_switch) to [facial recognition,](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_recognition_system) nearly 100 new state laws will take effect this week that will directly impact Connecticut residents.
#### Facial recognition In the fast-changing world of technology, the state legislature passed a package of consumer protections and privacy laws related to facial recognition, [artificial intelligence,](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence) chatbots, and surveillance pricing, among others.
James Maroney, a Milford Democrat who has worked on the issues since 2020, has spearheaded updates annually on data privacy and [artificial intelligence](https://www.cga.ct.gov/asp/cgabillstatus/cgabillstatus.asp?selBillType=Bill&which_year=2026&bill_num=5) — and he pledged to return to the state Capitol in 2027 [to update the laws](https://www.cga.ct.gov/asp/CGABillStatus/cgabillstatus.asp?selBillType=Bill&bill_num=sb4) as technology evolves and new issues arise.
In addition, companies must disclose their use of artificial intelligence if the technology is used to screen applicants for jobs.
